clues: This city lies by the Pacific shore in the south of a large west state. A huge city sits a short drive to the north-west.
In late spring, cool ocean air meets warm land air and forms a thick gray layer. Mornings in May and June turn dim and foggy.
At first this town had a plain name by the sea. In 1903 it took a new name, for Henry, a rich man of trade.
Waves roll in strong in both winter and summer at this shore town. That steady surf all year gave it the proud tag Surf City.
A smooth strip of sand runs for more than nine miles by the sea here. Crowds flock to its long shore for sun and surf all year.
